name: Aegis Logistics Ltd
tagline: A now-large-cap LPG/liquid/ammonia infrastructure compounder that its own longest-tenured holder explicitly calls 'never a 2x-in-a-year kind of stock' — plus a fresh $1.5B acquisition wildcard
business_overview: Aegis Logistics builds and operates LPG, liquid chemical, and ammonia storage/terminal infrastructure across Indian ports (Kandla, Pipavav, Mangalore, JNPT), largely through its ~45%-owned, separately-listed subsidiary Aegis Vopak Terminals (AVTL), plus a direct-to-consumer LPG distribution business (Cinkander, Magna brands). Management is targeting Rs 10,000 Cr gross block by FY27 at 20-25% target IRR on capex.
fundamentals_table: 14.77% (FY24 overall was 19%, Gas division 26%, Liquid division 13%)
Revenue +23% YoY to Rs 8,333 Cr, normalized EBITDA +36% to Rs 1,599 Cr, PAT +41% to Rs 1,107 Cr (first time crossing Rs 1,000 Cr PAT)
fundamentals_narrative: A genuine infrastructure-scale growth story: FY26 was a breakout year (revenue +23%, EBITDA +36%, PAT +41%, first Rs 1,000+ Cr PAT year), and Q1 FY27 continued strong despite Iran-war-related LPG supply disruption fears that ultimately didn't materialize into a setback. New LPG capacity at Mangalore and Pipavav has come online, tripling throughput potential, and an ammonia storage terminal at Pipavav (with a non-binding MoU with L&T for a green-ammonia project) adds a new growth vertical. On 18-Aug-2026, Aegis disclosed it is in advanced talks to acquire UAE's Tristar for $1.5 billion — a scale-changing move if it closes.

bull_case: Genuine breakout year: FY26 revenue +23%, EBITDA +36%, PAT +41%, crossing Rs 1,000 Cr PAT for the first time, with Q1 FY27 continuing the trend
Real infrastructure moat being built: new LPG capacity at Mangalore/Pipavav tripling throughput, ammonia terminal optionality with a large potential L&T green-ammonia partnership
The disclosed $1.5B Tristar acquisition talks (18-Aug-2026) are a fresh, material wildcard that could meaningfully change the company's scale and growth trajectory if it closes

bear_case: At Rs 46,913 Cr, this is now unambiguously a large-cap, and the community's own most experienced long-term holder explicitly frames it as a multi-year infrastructure compounder, not a fast-return stock — directly contradicting the multibagger-pace thesis this project screens for

One poster's own math (based on management's Rs 10,000 Cr gross block / Rs 2,500 Cr EBITDA FY27 target at a 20x EBITDA multiple) implies a ~Rs 50,000 Cr market cap by Sep 2027 — the stock is already trading near that level today, suggesting the well-known growth story may be largely priced in

Asset-heavy, multi-year execution risk (jetty construction, port berths, land parcels, pipeline connections) that the thread's own veteran holder describes as 'a very challenging business' structurally, despite the good long-term line of business
Trusted-user signal here is passive and undersized relative to this project's higher-conviction names — not a concentrated bet
verdict_headline: A genuinely strong large-cap infrastructure compounder, explicitly not framed by its own community as a fast-multibagger candidate
verdict_reasoning: Fundamentals are real and improving (FY26 breakout year, strong Q1 FY27, credible new capacity coming online), and there is no red flag.

However, at Rs 46,913 Cr this is squarely a large-cap, and the community's own most knowledgeable long-term holder explicitly and repeatedly frames Aegis as a 5+ year infrastructure compounder rather than a stock that can deliver outsized returns quickly — a direct, first-person contradiction of the multibagger-pace thesis.

The trusted signal available is passive (a long-held position mentioned in a list, not a fresh sized bet), so per this project's methodology there is no floor to apply and conviction rests on fundamentals plus community framing alone.

The disclosed Tristar acquisition talks are a genuine wildcard worth monitoring next quarter, but at this early, unconfirmed stage they aren't enough to override the size and community-framing evidence. Conviction set to Medium reflecting real quality without a fit for this project's specific extreme-return mandate; thesis_fit is 'neither'.

track_record.note: FY19-FY26 screener consolidated. Both revenue growth >=10% AND ROCE >=15% in the same FY: FY19, FY22, FY23. Reported revenue is LPG-price-linked trading and very lumpy (FY21 -46%, FY23 +86%, FY24 -18%), so the growth test is noisy; the cleaner read is ROCE drifting 17%->13% FY22->FY26 as the gross block builds toward Rs 10,000 Cr ahead of throughput. FY26 ROCE 13% misses the bar.

quality_metrics.note: FY26 ROCE 13% / ROE 16%. Borrowings Rs 4,150 Cr vs normalised EBITDA ~Rs 1,599 Cr FY26 (~2.3x, largely at the ~45%-owned AVTL level). CFO Rs 2,028 Cr FY26 but roughly matched by terminal capex, so FCF is thin-to-negative through the Rs 10,000 Cr gross-block build. Management targets 20-25% IRR on capex; ROCE currently falling as assets land ahead of the throughput ramp - capex_efficiency neutral pending the fill.
